notes: 08001407's section 8, the statement of significance, read end to end for the first time (issue #346) — all 39 pages, lines 4576-6253 of the extracted text. Most of what it names is already on pages from the section 7 inventory and the #310 prose-tail sweep, read in prior runs: this batch is only what survived a check against the existing corpus. The PROPERTY OWNERS subsection names the era's developers at length, but per the dossier's People section and this issue's own caution, that subsection is about owners and none of them is taken by name here — the building facts it carries (a use, a prior structure, a conflicting date) are kept, the owner's name is not.

findings.description: The Miles Brothers, film distributors, operated San Francisco's first film exchange in a building at this address from 1902 or 1903 until the building was destroyed in the 1906 earthquake and fire. It predates the rooming house built on the parcel in 1910.

citation.label: National Register of Historic Places nomination, Uptown Tenderloin Historic District (reference number 08001407), National Park Service.

raw.text: The first film exchange was located at 116 Turk Street in 1902 or 1903 by the Miles Brothers and was destroyed in 1906.

resolution.method: EAS exact match on 116 TURK ST → parcel 0339004; sf-parcels has blklot 0339004 active, 116–118 TURK; the 2025 roll records it as commercial hotel, built 1910. EAS puts 116, 118 TURK ST on that parcel, so per the directory contract the fact belongs on one page at the lowest, 116. The record was written in 2008, after the 1909 renumbering, so the number it gives is a modern number and the renumbering guard does not apply; the assessor dates the building on this parcel to 1910.

publish.note: New historical_record entry at 116 Turk Street: the pre-fire film exchange, distinct from the 1910 rooming house already on the page.
